questions.question: How many beats does a core module have?
questions.why: Five: Break, See, Fix, Prove and Keep. Concept modules use Lab and Check in place of Fix and Prove.

questions.question: Which beat proves a fix with numbers?
questions.why: Prove runs the old board and the new board on the same seeds and reports the pass rate.

options.text: Your settings next to what a run does
A chart of your typing speed

questions.question: What does your Harness Board show?
questions.why: It is the Turn Clock with a board: the harness's settings beside the run.

options.text: In the footer, with Export progress

questions.question: Where do you export your progress?
questions.why: The footer has Export progress, which saves a file you can import on another device.

options.text: Not necessarily: answers can vary from run to run

questions.question: Does a model give the same answer twice to the same prompt?
questions.why: Sampling makes answers vary, so one good run proves little about the next one.

options.text: The number of messages in a chat
The most text the model can read in one call
A browser tab that holds the chat

questions.question: What is a context window?
questions.why: Everything in one call, the prompt and the tools included, has to fit inside the window.

options.text: Everything from the last call, on its own
Only what the harness sends with the call
Whatever the provider saved for it

questions.question: What does a model carry from one call to the next?
questions.why: Tempting. The course shows what each call carries in A3.

options.text: A function the harness runs when the model asks for it

questions.question: Which of these is a tool?
questions.why: The model asks; the harness runs the function and returns the result.

options.text: It asks for tools, the harness runs them, and it calls the model again
It has a longer system prompt

questions.question: What makes a chatbot into an agent?
questions.why: The model asks, the harness acts, and the loop goes on until something stops it.

options.text: A turn limit or a token budget

questions.question: What stops a loop that never gets an answer?
questions.why: A turn limit and a token budget are exits the harness controls. A model's own stop is a claim.

options.text: Verification, with checks the harness runs
The user, who reads the answer

questions.question: What checks a done claim?
questions.why: A done claim is only a claim until a check runs and confirms it.

options.text: Send it back as the result, marked as an error

questions.question: A tool call returns an error. What should the loop do?
questions.why: The model can read the error and try again. Dropping it hides the problem.

questions.question: Which wire decides what stays in the context window?
questions.why: Context and memory decides what the model sees on each call.

questions.question: Which wire checks each tool request before it runs?
questions.why: Permissions checks each tool request before the tool runs.

questions.question: Which wire writes down each event, so a run can be read afterwards?
questions.why: Observability records each step, which is how a trace is made.
